To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

farnesoid-X-receptor (FXR)-ligands upregulate peroxisome-proliferator-activated-receptor (PPAR) γ mRNA expression in hepatic stellat cells (HSC), which in turn contributes to the antifibrogenic effects of FXR- and PPARγ-agonists in rodent models liver cirrhosis.
farnesoid-X-receptor (FXR), a nuclear receptor, is activated by bile acid and protects against liver fibrosis in rodent models.
FXR ligand treatment upregulates PPARγ mRNA and potentiates its antifibrotics effects in rodent models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel antifibrotics for the treatment of liver fibrosis based on the activation of the FXR-PPPARγ pathway.
the identification of novel molecular pathways that can contribute to the development of more effective therapeutic strategies for the treatment of liver cirrhosis.
a new mechanism of action for FXR ligands, which is independent of the classical FXR-PPRE pathway, and may be exploited to design new antifibrotics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FXR ligand treatment upregulates PPARγ in HSCs, and that this is an important mechanism by which FXR ligands inhibit HSC activation.
FXR ligand 6-ECD-CA up-regulates the expression of PPA Rγ in HSCs, and this effect is associated with a potent antifibrogenic activity in vivo.
FXR ligand 6-ECDAC, a potent FXR ligand, up-regulates PPARγ expression and activity in HSCs in vitro and in rodent model of liver cirrhosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FXR-PPRγ axis is an attractive target for the treatment of liver fibrosis in patients with chronic liver diseases.
FXR ligand 6-ECDAC reverses the suppression of PPAR-γ mRNA in activated HSCs and liver cirrhosis in rodent models.
the FXR-PPRγ cross-talk may provide a novel therapeutic strategy for liver fibrosis treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FXR and PPRγ ligands may have synergistic antifibrotice effects in rodent models, and this may have implications for the treatment of liver fibrosis in humans.

FXR ligand treatment may be a useful approach to treat hepatic fibrosis in humans, and that the combination of FXR and FXR/PPARγ ligands may be a useful strategy in the clinical treatment of patients with liver cirrhosis.
FXR ligand 6-ECDAC, which is currently under development for clinical use, can be used to potentiate the antifibrosis activity of PPARγ ligans.
